parts.name: plate 0

physics.Basic_description: Stack of dark grey rectangular metal plates with a matte finish, forming the main housing of the lock.
physics.Functional_description: Encases the locking mechanism and provides structural integrity to the lock body.
physics.Grasped_description: A gripper can grasp the sides of the stacked plates firmly to hold or manipulate the lock body.
physics.reason: The body is constructed from stacked plates that form a casing around an internal locking mechanism, creating a hollow volume rather than a solid block.

parts.name: rivet 0

physics.Basic_description: Small, silver-colored circular fasteners visible on the face of the lock body.
physics.Functional_description: Secure the stacked metal plates together to maintain the assembly of the lock body.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and flush to be grasped individually; they are part of the surface texture.
physics.reason: Rivets are small, dense metal fasteners that are solid throughout their volume.

parts.name: keyway disc

physics.Basic_description: Circular metallic disc surrounding the keyhole, appearing silver or light grey in the center of the body.
physics.Functional_description: Reinforces the key entry point and provides a wear-resistant surface for key insertion.
physics.Grasped_description: Flush with the surface and too small to be a primary grasp point.
physics.reason: The disc is a thin but solid metal component pressed into the body plate.

parts.description: Circular metallic disc surrounding the keyhole, appearing silver or light grey in the center of the body.
parts.function: Reinforces the key entry point and provides a wear-resistant surface for key insertion.

parts.name: keyway slot

physics.Basic_description: The central keyhole opening, appearing as a dark void or internal brass mechanism within the disc.
physics.Functional_description: Accepts the key to engage the locking mechanism.
physics.Grasped_description: An opening/void, not a graspable surface.
physics.reason: Represents the void of the keyway and the thin walls of the internal cylinder mechanism.

parts.description: The central keyhole opening, appearing as a dark void or internal brass mechanism within the disc.
parts.function: Accepts the key to engage the locking mechanism.

parts.name: shackle bar

physics.Basic_description: Thick, U-shaped white/silver metal bar extending from the top of the lock body.
physics.Functional_description: The locking element that passes through the hasp or chain to secure the equipment.
physics.Grasped_description: The primary handle for lifting or carrying the lock; easily grasped by the vertical legs or top arch.
physics.reason: Shackles are solid metal rods designed to resist cutting and pulling forces.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)
simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained
